questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: the academic level at the university, the selection of courses offered at the university,and the fact that I had never visited the country before

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: only due to personal issues, the services provided by the host university were great

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: As far as I remeber, everything was quite clear

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: there was an introduction event for exchange students with some useful information, and then the international student associations were helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: through Idealis and later subletting through facebook. I found it relatively easy, but a lot of people obviously struggle

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a really small town, so living off campus is not a big deal, but the further away from Wageningen city center, the more cut off you might feel

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't always easy to find courses - you really had to dig deep

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I honestly don't remember, but I was allowed into all courses and didn't have to put much effort in. Dennis was helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: support on determining whether courses were appropriate and whether I lived up to the prerequisites.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I reccomend not feeling obliged to follow a minor, if there are other courses that seem interesting to you outside the minor

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most courses were very stimulating and very progressive

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took several masters courses (also my 7th semester ) and was able to follow, whereas the bachelor course I took was a bit too introductuty

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: less personal, more professional, and more critical at WUR

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: introduction to GIS, CC economics & policy, Sustainable food systems, env. Justice and Communities Conservation and Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
all except env. justice which I found quite vague and too reliant on group work. 
Especially sustainable food systems was amazing.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sporta and social events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: join a sports team and student associations to gain a bigger network

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: visit the market every Saturday and all the second hand shops. go to the river when the weather is good.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, although dutch students stick to themselves a lot, including my roomies, so didn't get to know them too well

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: just that most dutch didnt seem very interested in befriending internationals

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the biking, the appreciation of nature, the culture around the market and the humor

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: that you shall prepare for long days at uni (sometimes 8-17), dothat sharing your time with friends is the best way to get you through the day, and not to postpone studying / readign till the exam period, as you often have deadlines then too.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's not as easy to get to amsterdam as you might think, so prepare to visit some smaller towns and also stay in Wageningen quite a bit

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: travelling around Europe and also the interesting, progressive education with a lot of new perspectives

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being lonely

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
